TurnRewindParams.description:
`turn/rewind`: run the conversation again from one of its turns — the reply to it is thrown
away and asked for once more, or (with `text`) the user's words are replaced first.

`turn_id` names the turn to run *again*, so a retry names the last one and an edit names the
one being corrected. Everything after it is dropped from the history; the transcript keeps
the lines and records a rewind marker, so nothing is destroyed on disk.

rewindFiles.description:
Put the workspace back to how it was before that turn's run first.

A retry that leaves the tree alone re-runs the prompt against code the abandoned attempt
already changed — it reads files the first run edited, or its patch finds the change
already applied and does nothing. Both are silent. The caller asks the user, so this is
never implied: `false` means "keep my files", which is what someone repeating a prompt
after their own edits wants.

text.description: Replacement words for that turn; absent keeps the ones it already has (a retry).

TurnSteerParams.description:
`turn/steer`: something the user says while a run is working.

Not a new turn and not a queued prompt: the words join the run that is in flight, at the top
of its next model request (codex's `turn/steer`). `expectedTurnId` is required and must match
the run that is live, so a steer can never land in a run the client did not mean — the answer
names the turn it actually found when they differ.

params.description:
`turn/rewind`: run the conversation again from one of its turns — the reply to it is thrown
away and asked for once more, or (with `text`) the user's words are replaced first.

`turn_id` names the turn to run *again*, so a retry names the last one and an edit names the
one being corrected. Everything after it is dropped from the history; the transcript keeps
the lines and records a rewind marker, so nothing is destroyed on disk.

rewindFiles.description:
Put the workspace back to how it was before that turn's run first.

A retry that leaves the tree alone re-runs the prompt against code the abandoned attempt
already changed — it reads files the first run edited, or its patch finds the change
already applied and does nothing. Both are silent. The caller asks the user, so this is
never implied: `false` means "keep my files", which is what someone repeating a prompt
after their own edits wants.

What a preview is. The kind decides the view, and every field that only one kind needs is
absent on the others rather than empty.

Why a preview failed. Every producer of a failure picks one, so the pane can draw the right

never becomes a base64 frame.

message.description: The conclusion, in words a reader acts on. Never an errno.

AppSettings.description:
What every client of this server shares about how the app looks. Ids name themes from the
clients' own catalog; one a client does not know falls back to its default.

aiLanguage.description: AI 偏好语言: the language every reply is asked to be written in, whatever the user types.

approvalPolicy.description: When the user is asked before something runs (codex's `approval_policy`).

autoArchiveAfterDays.description: Automatically archive inactive, unpinned conversations after this many days.

autoCompactionEnabled.description: Automatically summarize a conversation near its effective context capacity.

autoReviewApprovals.description:
Let the conversation's model review a command or patch that would ask for approval, and
answer it when the action is plainly fine or plainly not; anything unclear still asks.

browserDownloadDir.description: Local browser download directory. Empty uses the platform Downloads folder.

browserHomepage.description: Browser home page. `about:blank` is the default and HTTP(S) URLs are accepted.

browserUseSystem.description: Route agent browser actions to an isolated profile in an installed Chromium browser.

codeModeEnabled.description: JavaScript orchestration. Changes take effect at the next turn boundary.

collapseThinking.description: 折叠思考内容: fold finished thoughts into the tool batch they sit in. Display only.

computerClipboard.description: 读写剪贴板: allow the computer tools to read or replace the shared system clipboard.

computerControl.description:
允许操作电脑: the master switch for the desktop-control driver. Off, the driver is not
running and the agent has no desktop tools; on, the app that holds the OS permissions
runs it (`computer/host`).

computerPreferBackground.description: 优先后台投递: use the driver's background delivery route where it supports the action.

customSystemPrompt.description: User-authored suffix of each conversation's system instructions. Empty disables it.

glass.description: 玻璃效果: the translucent window, where the platform has a blur to show.

keepAwake.description: 运行时保持唤醒: on unless turned off, as in the desktop app.

notifications.description:
系统通知: tell the user when a run finishes, fails or waits for an answer while no
window has their attention.

proxyUrl.description: Optional HTTP(S)/SOCKS proxy used for model and catalog requests.

replySuggestions.description:
回复推荐: guess the user's next message and offer it as the composer's placeholder. On
unless turned off, like the Electron app's `replySuggestions`.

resourcePanelOpen.description:
会话资源: the docked resources panel beside the conversation is open. A narrow window
keeps the popover form, which only a deliberate open turns on.

sandboxMode.description: How much of the machine a command may touch (codex's `sandbox_mode`).

sandboxNetwork.description: Whether sandboxed commands may use the network.

toolSearchEnabled.description: 工具搜索: offer `tool_search`, so deferred tools can be found and loaded on demand.

uiFontSize.description: 界面字号: the root font size in px that every rem-based size scales from.

ApprovalPolicy.description: When the user is asked before something runs.

oneOf.description: Ask before anything that is not known to be read-only.
Run in the sandbox; ask only to run again outside it after it was in the way.
Run in the sandbox; the model asks when it needs to leave it.

total.description: Zero until every part's size is known.

ComputerStatus.description: Where the desktop-control driver stands on this machine.

binary.description: Where that executable is, for the application that runs it.

error.description: The last failure of an install, for the pane to show.

installed.description: The driver executable is in the data directory and its version is the one this build pins.

running.description: The host application has a driver daemon up and registered with this server.

supported.description:
Whether this OS and CPU have a driver build at all. `false` also covers a server running
with no desktop (the SSH Agent), which has nothing to control.

DirEntry.description: One row of a directory listing.

path.description: Absolute, so a client can ask for it back without knowing the tree's root.

Goal.description: A long-running objective attached to one conversation.

round.description: 1-based number of the round the agent is on.

GoalStatus.description:
Where a goal stands. A goal runs round after round by itself until the model declares it
done, the user pauses or stops it, or a round fails.

oneOf.description:
Audio returned by a tool. `data` is base64 so the same item works over the local and
remote transports without an extra media endpoint.
An image returned by a tool, carried as bounded base64 for the transcript viewer.

The conversation was summarized to make room; everything before this is no longer
sent to the model (but is still shown).

reason.description: `threshold`, `overflow` or `manual`; absent while it runs and on old transcripts.

model.description: Native provider/model label. None follows the default authenticated model.

QueueItem.description: One prompt waiting its turn: what the user typed while a reply was still being written.

at.description: When it was queued, by the server's clock.

QueuePauseReason.description:
Why the queue is standing still. Each one is a different sentence beside the prompts, and
only the user's own 继续 starts it again.

oneOf.description:
The user stopped the reply. The prompts after it were not meant to be abandoned, but
nothing should run without them saying so.
The reply failed. Sending the rest of the queue would feed a run that is already broken.

SandboxMode.description: How much of the machine a command may touch.

oneOf.description: Read anything; write in the project's folders and the temporary directories.

order.description: Each section owns its order: "pinned", "chats", or "project:<absolute path>".

ThinkingLevel.description: How hard the model is asked to think. There is deliberately no "off".

model.description: `provider/model` this conversation uses; the default model when absent.

pinned.description: Kept at the top of the sidebar.

source.description: Where a conversation came from when it was imported; ordinary conversations omit it.

worktree.description: The isolated checkout this conversation runs in, when it is bound to one.

at.description: When it happened, by the server's clock.

ThreadEvent10.description: `thread/notice`: a message the agent pushed to the user without waiting for a reply.

ThreadEvent11.description: `thread/goal/changed`: the goal as it now stands; `None` means it was cleared.

ThreadEvent12.description: A turn and everything after it was dropped, because it is running again (a retry or an edit).

ThreadEvent13.description:
回复推荐: what the user is likely to say next, offered as the composer's placeholder until they
type. `None` withdraws it — the guess was not worth showing, or a new run has made it stale.

ThreadEvent14.description:
A request to the client has been answered or withdrawn (by whichever client got there
first, or because the turn was stopped); every other client takes its prompt down.

ThreadEvent3.description: `running` is true from the moment a turn is accepted until it has fully settled.

durationMs.description: Exact server-measured duration for a completed reasoning item, in milliseconds.

ThreadEvent6.description: The model replaced its checklist. Each update is the whole list, not a change to it.

ThreadEvent7.description:
Whole-transcript totals survive compaction; `turn` starts at the latest user input.
Speed always pairs the latest completed assistant request's output with its own time.

cost.description: USD; absent until model pricing is known, never a guessed zero.

ThreadEvent8.description: How much of the model's context window the conversation takes. Summarizing starts at 90%.

ThreadEvent9.description: A conversation's queue, in the order the prompts will be sent.

pause.description:
Set when the queue stopped on its own: nothing is sent until the user says so. `None`
means it will drain as replies finish.

ThreadWorktree.description: The isolated checkout a conversation is bound to, instead of its project's own tree.

branch.description: The branch checked out there, or `HEAD` when detached.

TokenCounts.description: Cumulative uncached input/output and cache traffic. Cache writes are not cache hits.

oneOf.description: Stopped by the user (`turn/interrupt`). Not a failure.

UiLanguage.description: The desktop language. Chinese remains the default for existing installs.

WorkspaceEntryChange.description: Global workspace notification: invalidate listings, and remap open paths after a rename.

path.description: Old path for rename/delete; the new path for creation.

callId.description: The tool call it is for.

desktop app has. `action` is one of `open`, `snapshot`, `click`, `type`, `press`, `scroll`,

header.description: A short heading, 12 characters or fewer.

id.description: What the answer is filed under.

isOther.description: Offer a free-form "Other" answer besides the options.

serverRequest.description:
Server → client requests that wait for an answer. The client replies with a JSON-RPC
response carrying the result type named on each variant, or with an error to decline.

oneOf.description: Questions for the user; answered with a [`UserInputResponse`].
A command or patch that needs the user's say-so; answered with an [`ApprovalResponse`].
An action on the browser pane; answered with a [`BrowserResponse`].
